story.headline: Houthi strike on Riyadh airport kills 12
story.summary: An attack on Riyadh's King Khalid airport on 10 October killed 12 and injured 309; the Saudi-led coalition blamed the Houthis and Trump said the US may join strikes.
story.display_body: An attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on Saturday 10 October killed 12 people and injured 309, Saudi Arabia's General Authority of Civil Aviation said, and the Saudi-led coalition blamed Yemen's Houthis. The dead were four Saudis, two Bangladeshis and one national each of the US, Egypt, Jordan, Syria, Palestine and Sudan. A Saudi official told the Associated Press that a missile hit a passenger terminal. Al Jazeera calls it the deadliest attack on the kingdom in more than a decade, and the third on the airport this week. The Houthis have not formally claimed it. On Sunday 11 October their spokesman, Yahya Saree, warned travellers and airlines against using Saudi airports and airspace, which he called "a theatre of operations", while exempting the airports of Mecca and Medina. Coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki called the strike a "war crime" and promised to respond "decisively". The airport stayed closed into Sunday. US President Donald Trump said Washington "may" join Saudi strikes on the Houthis and would decide "very quickly"; Secretary of State Marco Rubio confirmed that an American was among the dead. UN Secretary-General António Guterres said attacks on civilian infrastructure violate international law.
story.why: the strike moves the Yemen war, which flared again during the US-Israeli war with Iran, onto civilian aviation in the Gulf's largest economy, and it raises the prospect of direct US involvement.

story.headline: Trump says Ukraine needs a new leader
story.summary: Trump said on 10 October Ukraine should replace Zelensky with a leader who can make a deal, a day after his Russian diesel deal.
story.display_body: US President Donald Trump said at the White House on Saturday 10 October that Ukraine should "get a new leader who can make a deal", a day after he announced the deal to release Russian diesel onto world markets. He said Volodymyr Zelensky had "lost 30% of your country". Independent estimates put the share of Ukraine under Russian control at about 20%, DW notes. Trump also repeated his warning to Kyiv: "do what you want" against Russia, but "don't hit refineries". For weeks Trump has blamed Ukraine's drone strikes on Russian refineries for high US fuel prices ahead of the Tuesday 3 November midterms. DW attributes the rise in those prices to his own war with Iran. Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev welcomed the remarks. Ukraine's foreign minister replied overnight that Zelensky "has the support of the people" and that Ukrainians choose their own leaders. RFI's correspondent in Kyiv reports that a large majority of Ukrainians think elections must wait until the war ends; nearly a million people are serving in the army. Zelensky said Russia had "thanked" Washington by dropping glide bombs on Zaporizhzhia on Saturday, where DW reports 20 people were killed.
story.why: Washington is now publicly calling for Ukraine's elected wartime leader to be replaced while easing sanctions on Moscow, which removes much of the US weight behind Kyiv in the talks.

story.headline: Pakistan suspends PTI-run Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government
story.summary: Pakistan's president imposed emergency rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on 11 October, suspending the provincial government of Imran Khan's PTI.
story.display_body: Pakistan's President Asif Ali Zardari placed Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province under emergency rule on Sunday 11 October, suspending the provincial government run by jailed former prime minister Imran Khan's party, the PTI. He acted on a recommendation from Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's cabinet. Sharif's office cited the "provincial government's deliberate disengagement from the fight against terrorism". The PTI denies sympathising with the Pakistani Taliban, which the government blames for a recent rise in attacks. PTI lawmaker Junaid Akbar said the province's chief minister, Sohail Afridi, and the party's provincial president were arrested shortly afterwards. The move comes as Khan's supporters prepare a march on Islamabad to demand his release; the government has blocked the routes into the capital with shipping containers. A PTI spokesman said the decision would lead to "further bloodshed". The president's office has not said how the province will be run.
story.why: suspending the one province held by the main opposition party removes its last seat of government power during a standoff over Khan's imprisonment.

story.headline: Djibouti shipwreck kills at least 109 migrants
story.summary: IOM said at least 109 migrants died and over 116 are missing after a boat bound for Yemen capsized off Djibouti on 8-9 October.
story.display_body: At least 109 migrants, 15 of them children, died and more than 116 are missing after a boat carrying about 350 people capsized off Djibouti on the night of 8–9 October, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) said on Sunday 11 October. IOM calls it the deadliest shipwreck off Djibouti. The boat sank near Guhere, north of Obock, on its way to Yemen. More than 80 people survived, all Ethiopian nationals, and IOM is caring for 64 of them. The route crosses the Bab el-Mandeb Strait to Yemen, which migrants try to cross to reach Gulf states. IOM has counted more than 20,000 arrivals in Djibouti from Ethiopia since 10 September. More than 900 people died or went missing on this route in 2025.
story.why: people keep taking this crossing even as the Yemen war intensifies on the other side.

story.headline: Abbas delays Palestinian elections to 2027
story.summary: Mahmoud Abbas postponed legislative elections set for 28 November to 11 September 2027, alongside the presidential vote.
story.display_body: Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas has postponed the legislative elections set for Saturday 28 November by almost a year, to Saturday 11 September 2027, the same day as the presidential vote. His decree cites "obstacles" from Israeli measures in the West Bank and East Jerusalem and the conditions in Gaza. RFI's correspondent reports widespread disillusionment among Palestinians, after elections were also called off in 2021. Abbas had confirmed the November date in his address to the UN General Assembly a few weeks earlier, and he has ruled by decree since his mandate expired in 2009. Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar called the decree "yet another ridiculous lie".

story.headline: Lausanne–Yverdon rail line reopens after arson
story.summary: SBB restored Lausanne-Yverdon rail traffic on 11 October after an arson attack on signalling cables at Eclépens disrupted the line from 9 October.
story.display_body: Rail traffic between Lausanne and Yverdon-les-Bains returned to normal at 05:40 on Sunday 11 October, after an arson attack on signalling cables at Eclépens (VD) had disrupted the line since Friday 9 October, the SBB said. The fire was found at about 03:00 on Friday in a cable duct beside the tracks. It destroyed the cables that control the region's rail installations and cut traffic between Cossonay-Penthalaz and Chavornay. Several long-distance trains were cancelled, and about a hundred SBB staff and twenty replacement buses were deployed. The SBB condemned the "criminal act" and will file a complaint against persons unknown; an investigation is under way.

story.headline: Crans-Montana to reserve CHF 5m a year
story.summary: Crans-Montana plans annual CHF 5 million reserves against civil claims over the Constellation fire; an expert puts the total bill above CHF 780 million.
story.display_body: The municipality of Crans-Montana (VS) plans to set aside CHF 5 million a year from 2026 against possible civil claims over the fire at the Constellation bar, which killed 41 people, according to minutes of its 29 April council meeting reported by Le Matin Dimanche on Sunday 11 October. Municipal president Nicolas Féraud said that funds would then be available "in ten to fifteen years" if claims lead to large payouts, and that the town would cut or postpone investments to build them up. The executive has admitted "shortcomings" in safety inspections, but its civil liability will only be decided after the criminal proceedings. Pascal Pichonnaz, a professor of private law at the University of Fribourg, estimates the total bill at at least CHF 780 million and possibly close to a billion, a figure he calls "necessarily still approximate".
story.why: Le Temps notes that the town is already heavily indebted, so if it cannot pay, the cost could fall on the canton of Valais and its taxpayers.

story.headline: Two more SVP names eye Parmelin's seat
story.summary: SVP national councillors Benjamin Giezendanner and Christian Imark do not rule out running to succeed Guy Parmelin after Esther Friedli withdrew.
story.display_body: SVP national councillors Benjamin Giezendanner (AG) and Christian Imark (SO) do not rule out standing to succeed Federal Councillor Guy Parmelin, the SonntagsZeitung reported on Sunday 11 October. Giezendanner said he would consider it if the party approached him, and Imark said he would if his profile met the requirements. SRF sources say some potential candidates had held back because they rated their chances low against St Gallen senator Esther Friedli, who withdrew on Friday 9 October. The SVP parliamentary group picks its ticket on Friday 20 November.
